text.p: Eurotunnel said in a restructuring prospectus presented on Thursday that it expected to show a net profit in 2005 and pay a first dividend the following year under a "base scenario".
Under a "lower case scenario", the Channel Tunnel operator would return to profit in 2006 and pay a dividend in 2010.
But if its financial performance improved faster than the base scenario, it could pay a dividend before 2006.

Under the base scenario and without an extension of the operating concession, Eurotunnel forecast pre-tax losses of 2,838 million francs ($493.6 million) for 1997, 2,358 million for 1998 and 1,819 million for 1999.
It reported a 6.1 billion franc loss for 1996.

Eurotunnel said in a statement issued at a news conference that if its results were below those expected in the lower case scenario, this would probably lead to a breakdown of the company's restructuring plan.
"Results inferior to those envisaged in the lower case scenario would probably lead to a breach of commitments taken by the group in the framework of the new bank agreement," the statement said.

Eurotunnel co-chairmen Patrick Ponsolle and Robert Malpas were quoted in the statement as saying: "This financial restructuring is the culmination of 20 months of intense and difficult negotiations. It constitutes, in the circumstances, a compromise acceptable to all the parties. Its implementation should allow the new team managing the group to devote all their efforts to improving its performance."
The prospectus sets out detailed terms and conditions for the restructuring of Eurotunnel's 69.4 billion francs of junior debt owed to banks.
The restructuring plan is being presented to the bank syndicate, which must approve it unanimously. It also requires majority shareholder approval.
Under the terms of the plan, the shareholders would hold 54.5 percent of Eurotunnel's capital after a capital increase.
Eurotunnel's concession to operate the Channel Tunnel expires in 2052. The company said it was pursuing talks for an extension of the licence. ($ = 5.749 French Francs)
